gaps.sentence: Come on, join ___ — it's easy once you start.
gaps.explanation: join in = take part in an activity others are doing.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to keep ___ with the latest slang.
gaps.explanation: keep up with = stay level with somebody/something changing.

gaps.sentence: You can count ___ me if you need help.
gaps.explanation: count on somebody = rely on them.

gaps.sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: Her honesty more than makes ___ for her lack of experience.
gaps.explanation: 'Make up for' = compensate for a shortcoming.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ off until Thursday.
gaps.explanation: 'Put off' = postpone to a later time.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of smoking, he finally managed to give it ___.
gaps.explanation: give up = stop/quit (a habit or attempt).

gaps.sentence: They want to try ___ the new software before buying.
gaps.explanation: try out = test something to see if it works.
